requirements.text: Classify shell work before applying rules: operator entrypoints go to internal-bash-script, sourced files and fragments stay here, and shell embedded in another format is claimed by that format's owner first.
requirements.source: internal-bash SKILL.md: When to use, Owner routing

requirements.text: Record the dialect contract, preserve the declared interpreter, and never recommend Bash syntax for a POSIX sh target.
requirements.source: internal-bash SKILL.md: Dialect decision, Bash branch, POSIX sh branch

requirements.text: Report review findings with the catalog ID, severity, location, and declared dialect; a finding that assumes the wrong dialect is not reported.
Validate changed shell with the bundle checker, which selects the dialect from the shebang or --dialect, returns 0, 1, or 2, and never executes the checked file.
Report the checker result as static evidence only; sh -n without dash is limited evidence and neither proves runtime behavior nor portability across every supported sh.
Report a catalog finding only when its stated condition holds in the reviewed code; code that meets the negative control is not a finding.
Apply Bash 3.2 rules only when the target is declared, and report compatibility as unverified unless a Python test harness executed the shell target under Bash 3.2 in an isolated workspace.

Write behavioral test setup, expected results, and assertions in Python using the existing Python framework. Shell fixtures, stubs, and invocation snippets may exercise the real target with its declared interpreter, but must not implement test assertions. Do not introduce Bats or a shell assertion harness.
Choose observable behavior and meaningful success, error, and boundary cases; derive expected results independently; isolate mutable state and preserve the declared framework.
Use focused native tests first, separate actual integration and declared compatibility checks, and justify speed changes with comparable measurements.
Provide executable test recipes that detect representative defects, keep bundle guidance self-contained, and distinguish structural evidence from runtime effectiveness.

cases.prompt: Validate this Bash helper before I merge it.
cases.initial_state: A Bash file with a bash shebang; shellcheck and dash are installed.
cases.expected_output: The checker passes the valid file with exit 0 and reports the defective file with exit 1 and SC2086 quoting findings.

assertions.text: The valid file returns 0 and the defective file returns 1.
The file is checked statically and never executed.

forbidden_actions: Run the checked file to validate it.

cases.prompt: This file ships as /bin/sh on Alpine. Is it safe?
cases.initial_state: A file with a #!/bin/sh shebang that uses local and [[ ]].
cases.expected_output: Keep the sh interpreter, report the Bash extensions as a dialect mismatch, and propose POSIX replacements; the checker returns 1 for the defective file and 0 for the valid one.

assertions.text: The answer does not switch the shebang to Bash.
Replacements use [ ] or test and no local or arrays.

forbidden_actions: Change #!/bin/sh to a Bash shebang without approval.

cases.prompt: Lint lib/common.sh; it has no shebang and is sourced by our Bash tools.
cases.initial_state: A sourced helper without a shebang, used only by Bash callers.
cases.expected_output: Record Dialect: Bash from the caller contract and run the checker with --dialect bash instead of guessing or adding a shebang.

assertions.text: The checker call passes --dialect derived from the caller contract.

forbidden_actions: Add a shebang to a sourced helper only to satisfy the checker.

pass: The transcript names the caller-provided dialect and shows scripts/check.sh --dialect bash.
fail: The agent adds a shebang or treats the checker's exit 2 as a lint finding.

cases.prompt: Review tests/evaluation/fixtures/posix-fragment.sh, a helper our /bin/sh entrypoints source, and list the problems.
cases.initial_state: The fixture is a POSIX sh function library sourced by #!/bin/sh callers.
cases.expected_output: A finding list that cites the unquoted expansions on lines 5 and 7 and the unguarded cd on line 5, each with catalog ID, severity, and line, under Dialect: POSIX sh.

assertions.text: Each finding carries a catalog ID, severity, and a line that exists in the fixture.
The unguarded cd and both unquoted expansions are reported.
No finding recommends [[ ]], arrays, or local for the POSIX target.

pass: Every reported line number maps to the cited defect in the fixture, and the dialect is stated as POSIX sh.
fail: A defect is missed, a line number is wrong, or a fix introduces Bash-only syntax.

cases.prompt: Write a new scripts/release.sh that operators run with --version and --dry-run.
cases.initial_state: No existing script; the request is a new operator entrypoint.
cases.expected_output: Route the work to internal-bash-script; this skill is at most an optional enrichment for its catalog and checker.

assertions.text: The operator entrypoint is handled by internal-bash-script.

pass: internal-bash-script owns the entrypoint; internal-bash appears only as an optional enrichment.
fail: The script is written using only internal-bash with no operator guidance.

cases.prompt: The run: step in .github/workflows/ci.yml fails on filenames with spaces; fix the shell.
cases.initial_state: A GitHub Actions workflow with a multi-line run: block.
cases.expected_output: Load the workflow owner first, then apply this skill only to the quoting semantics inside run:.

assertions.text: The workflow owner is loaded before shell rules are applied.

forbidden_actions: Change workflow triggers or permissions as part of a shell fix.

pass: The transcript loads the GitHub Actions owner and limits this skill to the run: shell.
fail: The agent treats the workflow file as a shell file and ignores the workflow contract.

cases.prompt: Confirm this POSIX helper is portable; dash is not installed on this Mac.
cases.initial_state: macOS host with /bin/sh as Bash in POSIX mode and no dash.
cases.expected_output: Report the checker pass as limited static evidence and name the missing check under each supported sh.

assertions.text: The answer does not claim cross-shell portability from sh -n.

pass: The report cites the limited-evidence line and lists the remaining evidence gap.
fail: The report states the helper is portable based on the macOS sh result.

cases.prompt: Check this POSIX helper that prints each entry of a list file.
cases.initial_state: Two #!/bin/sh helpers; shellcheck and dash are installed.
cases.expected_output: The checker returns 1 with SC2162 for the defective helper and 0 for the valid one; the review cites SH-M09 on the read line.

assertions.text: scripts/check.sh returns 1 for the defective fixture and 0 for the valid fixture.
The finding carries SH-M09 and the line of the read loop.

forbidden_actions: Run the checked file to validate it.

cases.prompt: Our log counter breaks on filenames with spaces; check the Bash helper.
cases.initial_state: Two Bash helpers with a bash shebang; shellcheck is installed.
cases.expected_output: The checker returns 1 with SC2045 for the defective helper and 0 for the valid one; the review cites SH-M10 and proposes a quoted glob with an existence guard.

assertions.text: scripts/check.sh returns 1 for the defective fixture and 0 for the valid fixture.
The finding carries SH-M10 and the line of the for loop.

forbidden_actions: Run the checked file to validate it.

cases.prompt: This helper must also run under the macOS system Bash. Is it compatible?
cases.initial_state: macOS host where /bin/bash --version reports 3.2; on any other host record the case as blocked. The fixtures only print text.
cases.expected_output: The checker returns 0 for both fixtures, so the answer does not treat it as compatibility proof. Under /bin/bash 3.2 the defective fixture exits 1 with an unbound-variable error and the valid fixture exits 0; the review cites SH-M12.

assertions.text: The answer states that the checker pass does not establish Bash 3.2 compatibility.
/bin/bash 3.2 exits 1 on the defective fixture and 0 on the valid fixture.
The finding carries SH-M12 and the empty-array expansion line.

forbidden_actions: Claim Bash 3.2 compatibility from the checker result alone.

cases.prompt: Review tests/evaluation/fixtures/review-new-ids.bash, a Bash helper library, and list the problems.
cases.initial_state: The fixture is a Bash helper library; each defect sits next to a negative control that handles the same concern correctly.
cases.expected_output: Findings SH-C04 on line 6, SH-C05 on line 14, SH-M11 on lines 25 and 29, and SH-m08 on line 38; the fixed-text sh -c on line 10, the digest check on line 20, and the explicit status check on line 33 are not reported.

assertions.text: Each listed defect is reported with its catalog ID, severity, and line.
None of the three negative controls is reported.
The sh -c finding uses SH-C04, not SH-C02.

pass: Every reported line maps to a listed defect, and no negative-control line appears as a finding.
fail: A listed defect is missed, a negative control is reported, or HTTPS alone is accepted as verification.

cases.prompt: Tidy up tests/evaluation/fixtures/posix-parity.sh; it runs under /bin/sh on Alpine.
cases.initial_state: The same fixture ships in internal-bash-script, whose C-DIALECT-PARITY case uses the same assertion IDs.
cases.expected_output: Record Dialect: POSIX sh, keep the #!/bin/sh interpreter, and propose no Bash-only syntax; the guarded glob is not reported.

assertions.text: The answer records Dialect: POSIX sh.
The #!/bin/sh interpreter is kept.
No change introduces [[ ]], arrays, local, or pipefail.

forbidden_actions: Change #!/bin/sh to a Bash shebang without approval.

pass: The same three assertions hold for this skill and for internal-bash-script on the shared fixture.
fail: The two skills reach different dialect decisions on the same fixture.

cases.prompt: Add regression tests for require_value in fixtures/valid/sourced-helper.sh. Our callers use Bash and our tests use pytest. Cover an empty value, a missing argument, and a value containing spaces. Change only test files.
cases.initial_state: A sourced helper without a shebang. require_value returns 1 and writes missing value to stderr for an absent or empty argument; a non-empty value succeeds. Bash and pytest are available.
cases.expected_output: Python tests pass values as subprocess arguments to a fixed Bash snippet that sources the helper and invokes require_value. Python asserts exit status and captured output for all three inputs; the helper is unchanged.

assertions.text: Setup, expected statuses, expected output, and assertions are Python code; the shell snippet only sources and invokes the target.
subprocess executes the real helper with Bash, preserving the spaced argument without interpolating it into shell source.
Missing and empty inputs each return 1 with missing value on stderr; the spaced non-empty input returns 0.

forbidden_actions: Introduce Bats or a shell assertion harness.
Modify the helper or add a shebang to it.

pass: The generated Python tests exercise all three real helper calls and independently assert their results.
fail: Expected-result comparisons appear inside the shell snippet, the helper is mocked, or a spaced value is split into multiple arguments.

cases.prompt: Test require_value in fixtures/valid/sourced-helper.sh for our POSIX sh callers. This repository uses Python unittest, not pytest. Keep dependencies and the helper unchanged.
cases.initial_state: The helper is sourced by /bin/sh. Python unittest is the existing framework. The shell target accepts a non-empty value and rejects an empty one.
cases.expected_output: Python unittest cases invoke the real helper through /bin/sh and assert both outcomes in Python, without adding pytest, Bats, or a shell assertion harness.

assertions.text: The tests use unittest and add no test dependency.
The helper is sourced and executed by /bin/sh, not silently switched to Bash.
Python assertions check success for a non-empty input and failure for an empty input; shell code contains no expected-result comparisons.

forbidden_actions: Replace the helper's declared caller interpreter with Bash.

pass: The generated unittest cases run both real inputs through /bin/sh and assert their statuses in Python.
fail: The tests introduce another framework, run only syntax checks, or put their assertions in shell code.

cases.prompt: Add useful fast Python tests for a shell target that receives a directory containing spaces and wildcard characters, invokes an external command, and must report command failures without corrupting files.
cases.initial_state: The repository already uses unittest with a stdlib harness. The shell dialect and deployment invocation are declared. The external command must not reach a live provider.
cases.expected_output: Keep unittest, execute the real declared shell boundary, pass inputs as arguments, use isolated workspace and environment with a bounded timeout, and verify quoted paths, command failures, and filesystem effects.

assertions.text: Tests execute the actual changed contract and detect at least one representative wrong result, wrong argument, or unintended side effect.
Mutable state is isolated and subprocess inputs, environment, working directory, and timeout are explicit when processes are needed.
Focused and broader evidence are distinguished; any claimed speed gain names comparable baseline and final measurements.

forbidden_actions: Assert instructional wording instead of behavior.
Migrate a working framework without authorization.
Claim runtime effectiveness from schema validation.

pass: A reviewer can identify the defect each test detects.
Relevant observable outputs and file effects are checked with isolated state.
Dependencies and supported runtime gaps are reported; optional speed machinery is evidence-based.
fail: Tests assert only mock presence or implementation source.
Tests inherit uncontrolled mutable home or shared output files.
Performance or model effectiveness is claimed without observed evidence.

cases.prompt: A refactor preserves the public contract, but tests fail because private helper names changed. Another test passes although the output artifact is no longer written. Repair the tests without introducing a new framework or broad fixture layer.
cases.initial_state: Existing native tests and an established public output contract; compatibility requirements are explicitly declared.
cases.expected_output: Keep real contract coverage, replace private structure assertions with independent result and side-effect checks, preserve framework and layout, and run focused then relevant broader checks.

assertions.text: The missing artifact causes a test failure while a behavior-preserving private refactor does not.
Shared fixtures or parallel execution are introduced only with isolation and measured cost justification.

forbidden_actions: Weaken the artifact contract to make the suite pass.

pass: Contract-preserving internal changes keep assertions valid.
A representative missing output defect is detected.
fail: The expected value is computed by the implementation being tested.

queries.query: Review lib/log.sh, the helper every tool sources, for quoting bugs.
Is `local` safe in this function that runs under /bin/sh on Alpine?
Harden the shell snippet in our Dockerfile RUN line that downloads and extracts a tarball.
Run shellcheck on the sourced functions in tools/common.sh and fix what it finds.
Does this pipeline need pipefail? It is a Bash fragment inside a Make recipe.
Replace the mktemp and trap logic in this sourced helper so temp files are cleaned up.
Explain why `[ $x = y ]` breaks when x is empty in our POSIX helper.
Check the quoting in the bash one-liner inside this workflow run: step.
Convert this Bash-only helper library to POSIX sh so BusyBox can source it.
Create a new deploy.sh that operators run with --env and --dry-run.
Add --help and argument parsing to our backup launcher script.
Fix the missing .PHONY targets in the Makefile.
Change the workflow trigger so CI runs on tags only.
Rewrite this Python CLI to use argparse subcommands.
Fix the YAML indentation in the pre-commit config.
Reduce the Docker image size by switching to a distroless base.
Make our operator-facing install.sh print a progress summary at the end.
Set up my zsh prompt theme in .zshrc.
Why is `cd dir && rm -rf *` risky inside a sourced cleanup function?
Review the PR diff as a whole before merge.
